To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we find a high fraction of disturbed velocity field in distant galaxies and the disturbed galaxies are found in both cluster and field environments.
we find no difference between the fraction of disturbed galaxies in cluster and field, and that the fraction of disturbed objects increases towards low masses.
we have measured the stellar masses of 92 galaxies out to z = 0. 5 and that the majority have stellar masses below the characteristic mass of the Schechter function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of galaxies in the early Universe and their evolution in the cluster environment.
the formation and evolution of galaxies in the nearby and distant universe.
the evolution of the structure and kinematic of galaxies in different environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cluster galaxies do not show significantly more disturbed velocity fields and morphologies than their field counterparts.
the environmental effect is not as strong as expected, but we may still be witnessing its early phase of evolution.
environmental effects are not the main driver for the formation of galaxies, but they can influence the evolution of galaxies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of galaxies in the distant universe are forming their stellar disks by accretion and minor mergers.
the evolution of the stellar and gaseous components is similar in the field and clusters, but that the latter may suffer from additional environmental influences.
the evolution of spiral galaxies is not significantly affected by the environment in our studied clusters at least until z ˜0.5.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evolution of galaxies in the field and in clusters is similar.
galaxies at z ˙ 0.5 are still in the process of building up their stellar disks.
we can now study the evolution of galaxy structures and kinematics in a consistent way out to z ˜0.5.
